label: DEMO: a fictional Second Brain deployment and the exports taken from it, for testing the import (SB-P8-01, SB-P8-02). Every person, place, company, number and host is invented.
notes: Times are ISO 8601 in UTC here; upstream stores and exports them as Unix milliseconds.
Columns are upstream's (db/schema.sql and the runtime columns of src/db/init.ts); key, note and expect are this fixture's own.
Users carry no token hash, suspension, default share or last-seen time: nothing the import reads, and a token hash is credential-shaped.
Events list what an import must account for; a real deployment also records a created event for every memory. Payloads keep only the fields an import reads.
Versions are full copies of the earlier text (prior_length is null), and exist only from the 4.0 upgrade on, as upstream's do.
expect says what upstream does with a row (held or served) and what Rhythm's import should do (held, served, or open where SB-P8-01 still decides).

entries.workspace_id: which workspace (personal, Family or a team) holds the memory: the import puts every memory in the importing person's private scope until a reviewed scope map moves it (D-049)
entries.actor_id: who wrote it: the importing person becomes the author, and a former member's or the system's authorship is lost
entries.when_at: a due date, event time or wake time: not restored; the tags that mark commitments, decisions and standing instructions are kept
entries.when_kind: whether when_at is due, event or wake: lost with it
entries.when_source: whether when_at was stated, found by a pattern or by a model: lost with it
entries.when_label: the due date's own words: lost with it
entries.staleness_checked_at: when the staleness pass last looked: lost; the stale:as-of tag is kept
entries.vector_ids: deliberately left out by upstream: deployment-specific; the import indexes again

edges.id: the edge's own id: an edge is known by its two ends and its type
edges.workspace_id: which workspace the edge belongs to, which follows a shared memory: an edge whose other end is outside the export names a memory the importer cannot see

projects.workspace_id: which workspace owns the project: the same slug can be in two workspaces of one export, and the import cannot tell them apart

tables.users: the members, their roles and who has left
tables.workspaces: the personal and team workspaces and their names
tables.entry_versions: earlier text, tags, dates and validity: history starts at the import (VER-11)
tables.entry_events: the audit trail: shares, edits, holds, status changes, deletions
tables.entries_trash: forgotten memories still in the trash: not exported, not imported
tables.prompt_capsule_revisions: the capsules' revision counters; the capsule tags on memories are kept
tables.insight_candidates: pairs waiting for the weekly insight pass
